funding.excerpt: The company is only 13 months old and has won approximately $60,000 from business plan competitions across the country, including taking second at the G. Steven Burrill Business Plan Competition in May.

April 6 (Reuters) - Fetch Rewards, a shopping rewards app backed by SoftBank Group's Vision Fund 2, has raised $240 million in a funding round that valued the company at more than $2.5 billion, Chief Executive Officer Wes Schroll told Reuters on Wednesday. The fresh capital, consisting of both equity and debt, came after the app doubled its active users base in the past year to 13 million. The latest round, led by investment management firm Hamilton Lane, brought the app's total funding to $578 million, and existing investors including Vision Fund 2, ICONIQ Capital and DST Global also participated.

companies.excerpt: Buffalo Automation, an artificial intelligence (AI) startup that is developing technology for self-navigating boats, has secured $900,000 in seed funding. The company, led by CEO and co-founder Thiru Vikram, was founded in 2015 by UB engineering students.

founders.name: Thiru Vikram
founders.affiliationRole: University at Buffalo engineering student; Buffalo Automation co-founder and CEO. Took a leave of absence from UB.
founders.verificationNote: University at Buffalo, 12 April 2018, names Thiru Vikram as CEO and co-founder of Buffalo Automation, founded by UB engineering students, and says he took a leave of absence from UB. No class year is printed.
founders.excerpt: The company, led by CEO and co-founder Thiru Vikram, is currently piloting its AutoMate system. Buffalo Automation, which was founded in 2015 by UB engineering students. The founders — including Vikram, who has taken a leave of absence from UB to focus on the startup full time.

funding.excerpt: Buffalo Automation has secured $900,000 in seed funding from investors. Buffalo Automation’s latest funding round was led by the Jacobs Family, owners of Delaware North, through their investment vehicle Deeridge Group LLC. Other investors included Gerald Lippes, Ted Pierce, and John Somers. Z80 Labs made a follow-on investment of $100,000.

The company has quickly gained recognition as one of the region’s promising startups, winning UB’s Henry A. Panasci Jr. Technology Entrepreneurship Competition (Panasci TEC) in 2016 and securing a $25,000 investment from Launch NY and Z80 Labs the same year.

companies.name: BRCĒ
companies.description: Performance materials company, including shoelaces meant to stay tied, built by Michigan State students Madhav Aggarwal and Tanvi Gadamsetti.
companies.excerpt: Michigan State University student entrepreneurs Madhav Aggarwal and Tanvi Gadamsetti, co-founders of BRCĒ, secured a $300,000 investment during their appearance on ABC’s Shark Tank, which aired on March 4, 2026. BRCĒ, pronounced brace, is a performance materials technology company built by Aggarwal and Gadamsetti while studying at MSU.

companies.name: Novoflow
companies.excerpt: In his sophomore year at Emory University, Rihet came across a LinkedIn post by Georges Casassovici. Their startup Novoflow is building AI agents for medical clinics. The company has just raised $3.1 million in funding, led by super angel Justin Hamilton, with participation from N1 Ventures, Multifaceted Capital, and Standard Partners Fund.

founders.name: Mathieu Rihet
founders.affiliationRole: Emory University sophomore who left school to build Novoflow
founders.verificationNote: Business Insider, 3 November 2025, says Mathieu Rihet was an Emory sophomore, dropped out after Y Combinator accepted Novoflow, and does not plan to return. This clears an earlier current-student label.
founders.excerpt: Nineteen-year-old Mathieu Rihet initially wanted to be a cardiothoracic surgeon. In his sophomore year at Emory University, Rihet came across a LinkedIn post by Georges Casassovici. Both dropped out of school after being accepted into Y Combinator's Spring 2025 class. Neither of the founders plan to return to school, Rihet told Business Insider. Their startup Novoflow is building AI agents for medical clinics.
